video.anchor: the book's isosceles triangle ABC with the height AD
maths_rules: isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC, AD perpendicular to BC; triangles ADB and ADC have AB = AC, a common side AD and right angles at D, so BD = DC and they match
turning ADC over and fitting its slanting side onto AB with the ends swapped is a half turn of ADB about the midpoint of AB, which gives a rectangle with sides BD and AD
the acute angles at A and at B add up to 90 degrees, so each corner of the new figure is a right angle
area = BD × AD = 1/2 × BC × AD, the area of the triangle

final_answer.value: cut along the altitude and join the two right triangles along their slanting sides to make a rectangle BD by AD

Turn ΔADC over and place it against ΔADB with the hypotenuses together.
The two right triangles form a rectangle with sides BD and AD, area 1/2 × BC × AD.

item.question: A slanting trapezium has parallel sides AB = 6 cm and DC = 10 cm and height 5 cm. Use Approach 2 to find its area.

Triangle BGC has base 10 − 6 = 4 cm: 1/2 × 4 × 5 = 10 cm².
item.text:
Worked example: A slanting trapezium has parallel sides AB = 6 cm and DC = 10 cm and height 5 cm. Use Approach 2 to find its area.
1. Parallelogram ABGD: 6 × 5 = 30 cm².
2. Triangle BGC has base 10 − 6 = 4 cm: 1/2 × 4 × 5 = 10 cm².
3. Total = 30 + 10 = 40 cm², and 1/2 × 5 × (6 + 10) = 40 cm².
Answer: 40 cm²

extra_items.question: Trapezium WXYZ has WX = 5 units, ZY = 9 units and height 4 units, with ZM = 2 and NY = 2. Find its area.
steps: Rectangle WXNM: 5 × 4 = 20.
Each end triangle: 1/2 × 2 × 4 = 4.
extra_items.text:
$1$. Rectangle $WXNM$: $5 \times 4 = 20$.
$2$. Each end triangle: $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4 = 4$.
$3$. Total $= 4 + 20 + 4 = 28$, and $\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times (5 + 9) = 28$.
Answer: $28$ square units

item.question: Find the areas of the following figures: (i) a trapezium with parallel sides 10 ft and 7 ft and height 16 ft between them, (ii) parallel sides 24 m and 36 m, height 14 m, (iii) parallel sides 14 in and 6 in, height 10 in, (iv) parallel sides 12 ft and 18 ft, height 8 ft.
item.text:
$1$. (i): $\frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times (10 + 7) = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 17 = 136\text{ ft}^2$.
$2$. (ii): $\frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times (24 + 36) = \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 60 = 420\text{ m}^2$.
$3$. (iii): $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times (14 + 6) = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 20 = 100$ in$^2$.
$4$. (iv): $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times (12 + 18) = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 30 = 120\text{ ft}^2$.
Answer: (i): $136\text{ ft}^2$ (ii): $420\text{ m}^2$ (iii): $100$ in$^2$ (iv): $120\text{ ft}^2$
